eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The retrospective cohort of adult lung transplant recipients uses a non‑linear machine learning CT analysis to predict graft survival, meeting population, AI intervention, outcome, and study design criteria.

identification_methods.Setting: Single-centre retrospective study at a tertiary academic transplant centre
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of adult first double lung transplant recipients with chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) using machine learning CT texture analysis and radiologist scoring.
identification_methods.Institution: University Health Network, University of Toronto
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included all adult first double lung transplant patients transplanted between Jan 2010 and Dec 2015 who developed CLAD and had a thin‑section inspiratory CT within 100 days after CLAD onset (or ≤28 days before). Excluded single lung, heart‑lung transplants and re‑transplants.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: CALIPER‑based lung texture analysis tool (Imbio Lung Texture Analysis) performing voxel‑wise classification into normal, hyperlucent, ground‑glass, reticular or honeycomb textures.
identification_methods.Input Variables: Machine learning outputs: percentages of hyperlucent lung, ground‑glass opacity, reticular texture, pulmonary vessel volume (PVV), total lung capacity (CTTLC). Radiologist scores: consolidation, ground‑glass opacity, reticulation, pleural effusion, air trapping, bronchiectasis.
identification_methods.Validation Method: Internal performance assessment using ROC curve analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression; no separate external validation set.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: CT scans acquired on Aquilion scanners at Toronto General Hospital; segmentation succeeded in 93% of cases. Statistical analyses performed in R version 4.0.

population.Inclusion criteria: All adult first double lung transplant patients transplanted between January 2010 and December 2015 who developed chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) and had an inspiratory CT near CLAD diagnosis
population.Exclusion criteria: Single lung transplants, heart–lung transplants, re‑transplants, patients who died without CLAD, CLAD‑free up to 31 December 2019, non‑CLAD pulmonary function decline, and those without a qualifying CT within the required time window
population.Target Population: Lung transplant recipients with chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD)
population.Population Notes: Retrospective single‑centre study; CT performed a median of 9.5 days from CLAD onset

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Inspiratory thin-section CT images at CLAD onset
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline CT at CLAD diagnosis
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Machine learning tool quantified ground-glass opacity, reticulation, hyperlucent lung and pulmonary vessel volume; segmentation successful in 93% of cases; tool not previously trained on transplant cohort
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Phenotype discrimination (AUC), graft failure prediction (hazard ratios)
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Both machine learning and radiologist scores predicted graft failure; PVV had highest AUC (0.85) for RAS/mixed phenotype and HR 1.23 for graft failure
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Focus on PVV as strongest diagnostic and prognostic biomarker; ROC analysis provided AUC values for multiple textures
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Hazard ratio for graft failure per unit increase in pulmonary vessel volume proportion
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: PVV was the strongest independent predictor of graft failure, independent of CLAD phenotype
